items.title: Why is Ukraine so reliant on Starlink and can Europe plug the gap?
items.description: Ukraine needs another satellite internet service, but a decent alternative to Elon Musk's network doesn't exist - yet.

items.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
items.description: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

sections.title: Beyond Climate & EU — World News Highlights

items.title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
items.description: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

items.title: Gadi Eisenkot campaigns on Moroccan roots in challenge to Netanyahu
items.description: As Israel prepares to vote, Gadi Eisenkot is leveraging his Moroccan heritage in Likud strongholds such as Sderot. From historical divides to October 7, identity and trauma are redefining the city's political loyalties.

items.title: Bulgaria holds presidential elections amid divisions over Ukraine war
items.description: Bulgarians are voting in presidential elections amid security concerns over attacks on ships in the Black Sea. The vote for the largely ceremonial post is seen as a test of the popularity of Prime Minister Rumen Radev.
